workflow_runs.display_title: fix: prevent orphaned rg processes in grep_files tool handler

head_commit.message:
fix: prevent orphaned rg processes in grep_files tool handler

The grep_files tool handler spawns `rg` (ripgrep) as a child process via
`tokio::process::Command::output()`, but unlike the general-purpose
spawner in `spawn.rs`, it was missing critical process management
configuration:

- `kill_on_drop(true)`: ensures the child is killed when the handle is
  dropped (e.g., on timeout cancellation), preventing orphaned processes
- `stdin(Stdio::null())`: prevents rg from hanging on its stdin-reading
  heuristic, consistent with the existing comment in `spawn.rs`
- Explicit `stdout/stderr(Stdio::piped())`: makes stdio handling explicit
  rather than relying on defaults

Without `kill_on_drop(true)`, when the 30-second timeout fires and the
future is dropped, the rg process could continue running indefinitely.
Over multiple tool invocations this leads to accumulated orphaned rg
processes consuming significant CPU, as reported in #7572 and #10846.

Fixes #7572
Refs #10846

head_commit.message:
fix: flaky test (#11428)

stage1_concurrent_claims_respect_running_cap was flaky due to SQLite
lock contention, not cap logic correctness. The claim flow used deferred
transactions (BEGIN) with read-then-write behavior, which can fail under
concurrency with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT/database is locked when upgrading
a read transaction to a write transaction. We fixed this by using BEGIN
IMMEDIATE for stage1 and phase2 claim paths, so lock acquisition happens
up front and contenders serialize cleanly instead of failing during
upgrade. After the change, codex-state tests pass and stress reruns of
the flaky path no longer reproduced the failure.
